To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the expression pattern and projections of embryonic zebrafish hypocretin/orexins (Hcrt) are similar to those in mice, 2) zebrafish display robust locomotor activity and rest behaviors, 3) Hcrt-overexpression in zebrafish promotes and consolidates locomotor activity and inhibits rest, and 4) Hcrt function does not require normal oscillations in locomotion.
The expression pattern and axon projection of zebrafish hypocretin neurons are strikingly like those of mice and that hypocretin overexpression in zebrafish induces an insomnia-like phenotype.
Zebrafish larvae have sleep-like behavior that is regulated by Hcrt.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic and molecular regulation of sleep in zebrafish and the identification of novel genes and neural circuits that regulate sleep and arousal in vertebrates.
the development and application of the zebrafish as a model organism for studying the genetics of sleep.
understanding the genetic and neural mechanisms that regulate sleep in zebrafish and mammals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the zebrafish is a good model for sleep studies.
the Hcrt overexpressing zebrafish is a model for insomnia, a disorder that has a significant impact on the health of millions of people.
the zebrafish has a similar expression pattern and function as the mammalian hypocretin/orexins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Hcrt is an arousal promoting neuropeptide that is involved in the regulation of wakefulness and sleep in zebrafish.
we have developed a zebrafish insomnia model.
Hcrt promotes and consolidates waking and inhibits rest in zebrafish and this effect is independent of circadian oscillations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Hcrt system in zebrafish and mammals is highly conserved and that Hcrr overexpression in zebrafis larvae results in an insomnia-like phenotype.
zebrafishes are an excellent model system for studying the genetic regulation of wakefulness and sleep.
the Hcrt system in zebrafish is similar to that in humans, and that zebrafishes can be used as a model to study Hcrt function.
